summary:
This bill makes appropriations for the Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, and related agencies for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2024.

For the Office of the Secretary and General Departmental Management within HHS, the bill provides $402,341,000, plus an additional $58,028,000 from PHS Act §241 for national health and human services research and evaluation. It allocates $28,000,000 for minority AIDS prevention and treatment, and $40,000,000 for competitive grants exclusively implementing sexual risk avoidance education, defined as voluntarily refraining from non-marital sexual activity. These grants must use medically accurate, peer-reviewed information and an evidence-based approach, teaching self-regulation, success sequencing, healthy relationships, goal setting, and resistance to coercion, violence, and youth risk behaviors, without normalizing teen sexual activity. No more than 10% of these funds may go to technical assistance or administration. The bill also provides $5,000,000 for prize competitions on kidney disease prevention, diagnosis, and treatment under the Stevenson-Wydler Act.

For Medicare Hearings and Appeals, the bill provides $196,000,000, of which $40,000,000 remains available through September 30, 2025, transferred from the Federal Hospital Insurance and Supplementary Medical Insurance Trust Funds. The Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT receives $56,238,000 from PHS Act §241 for interoperable health information technology grants, contracts, and cooperative agreements. The HHS Office of Inspector General receives $80,000,000, covering protective services for the Secretary and child support non-payment investigations. The HHS Office for Civil Rights receives $32,000,000. Retirement pay and medical benefits for Public Health Service Commissioned Officers are funded at such amounts as may be required.

The bill includes numerous general provisions (§§201–248) that impose conditions on the use of funds. It caps extramural grant salaries at Executive Level II, with an exception allowing NIH to pay up to 100% at that rate. It permits up to 2.5% of appropriated program funds for evaluation and allows transfers of up to 1% between HHS appropriations, with no appropriation increased by more than 3% and 15-day advance notice to the Appropriations Committees. Title X family planning applicants must certify that they encourage family participation for minors and provide counseling on resisting sexual coercion, and Title X providers are not exempt from state laws requiring reporting of child abuse, molestation, rape, or incest. No funds may be used to advocate or promote gun control. No Medicare Advantage plan may be denied participation for refusing to provide or refer for abortions, with the Secretary required to make actuarial adjustments to capitation payments accordingly. The bill permits up to 60 PHS employees to be assigned to child survival and AIDS programs through USAID, UNICEF, or WHO. It grants the HHS Secretary authority equivalent to the State Department for international health activities, including facility acquisition abroad and foreign service-equivalent benefits. NIH may transfer up to 3% among institutes and centers for HIV research, and up to $100,000,000 in NIH funds may be used for facility alteration, repair, or improvement, with no single project exceeding $5,000,000. BARDA is authorized to enter multi-year contracts of one to ten program years for research services and security countermeasures, with specific obligation and termination requirements. The bill also restricts official reception and representation expenses to $50,000 or less.

Under Section 529, funds provided for research, evaluation, or statistical purposes to the Administration for Children and Families, the Chief Evaluation Office, and the Bureau of Labor Statistics are available for obligation through September 30, 2028.
